pr_body:
When Replica is being destroyed, it can set tenantLimiter to nil. However, all accessors assume synchronization through IsInitialized atomic check and that this field can't be modified after the replica is initialized.

There is no particular need in nullifying this limiter, the replica is going away soon, so this commit removes this line in order to fix the data race.

Fixes #95345
Epic: none
Release note: none

@pavelkalinnikov This is related to the replica lifecycle work y'all are working on, can you pick this up?

review_comments:
Does this strictly prevent the race? The other end may notice the closed channel too late, and still write to the metric, no?

I wonder if the proper solution to this would be ref-counting at the request level. I.e. make it so that `Send` gets a ref-incremented `Limiter`, and `Releases` it in the end; instead of relying on `Replica` to do so.

Ah, I see, we rely on the fact that there is only one `Gauge` metric which also happens to be related to synchronization. We close the channel, and then some time after the waiters decrement the counter. In the meantime, we only `Unlink`. The counter eventually will stabilize.

Any generic gauge addition would break things again. Worth noting this and TODOing.
👍🏽 Did you want to add a TODO?
I think you covered it well in the comment next to `r.tenantLimiter`. Injected a TODO there.
Could we have a method instead?
I'm not opposed, your PR after all! For me personally this is ok as is.

Alternatively, we could protect `tenantLimiter` with `Replica.mu`, but I don't see much benefit. WDYT?

Technically, a few in-flight `Send`s can update this `tenantLimiter` after it has been released by `r.store.tenantRateLimiters.Release(r.tenantLimiter)`, but I wonder if that's ok.

Both options seem a little iffy. I don't want us to introduce another mutex acquisition in the critical path but at the same time it's not trivial to rearrange the users of this into an existing critical section.

Use-after-Release on the `tenantLimiter` might work - I looked at the code a bit and it seems like it doesn't destroy or pool any memory; it really just unlinks the limiter from the parent.

Let's go with the second option (the one you have chosen) but add a test in `tenantrate` that proves that you can use a limiter after it's been released and that this will not crash and also no longer influence the surrounding aggregating metric.

I wrote a test (see second commit; it fails). It does not panic after `Release`, but the parent metric is still updated. The `Destroy` method removes the child metric from the parent's tree, but still leaves the child->parent reference and keeps updating the parent metric. This API doesn't quite make sense to me, but it is what it is.

I think it's fine for counter metrics if some in-flight `Inc`rements slip through, but with the `Gauge` metrics we can't reliably reset it to 0 (and update the parent so that it no longer accounts for this value), a racing change may result in a permanent non-zero leak to the aggregate.
I don't know, but the whole fact that `Send` can race with `Replica` destruction, and operate on a half-destroyed one, seems iffy.

I think that the `Replica` "state machine" is confusing. Many things assume that there are only 2 states: uninitialized and initialized (hence the `IsInitialized` checks in many places, including `Send`, and assumption that many things synchronize through this check), but in reality there is also `destroyStatus` which breaks this dichotomy.

W.r.t. `Send`, I think it would make sense to drain/cancel all the sends before destroying the `Replica`. Then, at least for sends, the uninitialized/initialized assumption would hold.

> I think that the Replica "state machine" is confusing.

Yeah the in-memory lifecycle of a Replica is messy. I've had a few starts at trying to fix this but never managed to follow through[^1].

This isn't really a fight we can pick right now, though. We need to find some interim solution. You're right about the gauge presenting a problem. It's accessed only here:

https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/61674bc51ae20005b9fde0bd548c4c4a4f2e9e1c/pkg/kv/kvserver/tenantrate/limiter.go#L94-L103

I added some commits, PTAL. They basically try to make what is happening here safe: you can use the metrics for however long you want. They'll keep updating the parent, etc. For a gauge, it's your job to make sure that paired updates always happen in the pair. (This isn't really a new constraint). It was trivially true.

There's one major change here which we still need to vet, though. Previously, when `Destroy()`ing a gauge, we'd reset it to zero. This actually means that callers that do the right thing (decrement after you incremented no matter what happened in between) got a wrong value out in the end. It seems like the wrong kind of band-aid to reset the gauge here, but there are a bunch of users and it's unclear to me which of them, if any, relied on this behavior.

The reset was there from the start[^2]. Maybe @ajwerner has some intuition on whether we must absolutely keep that reset in place. It seems better to let whoever has a pending gauge update "drain out" themselves, or every user of aggmetric needs to have elaborate synchronization.

[^1]: https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pull/9450
[^2]: https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/commit/ce963b3e05da5e225017589742ed16a73639711a#diff-07ef90c24a6e27509cd532e4692cc1661c04eb05be44f2f9b5911ce046e95b6bR109-R114
